text: A model's weights don't change after launch, but the world feeding it does. That's often enough for accuracy to quietly decline — no error thrown, nothing visibly broken.
Data drift is the distribution of the input changing. Concept drift is the relationship between input and correct output changing — what used to count as a good answer shifting over time.
A real drift report compares a reference distribution against a current window, column by column, with a statistical test chosen per column — flagged Detected or Not Detected, with a drift score.
Opening a flagged column shows exactly how the shape changed, not just that it did — the reference distribution next to the current one, overlaid.
A report nobody checks gets ignored. The same checks as a pass/fail test suite turn drift into something a pipeline can act on automatically, naming the exact column that crossed the threshold.
The same idea works for an LLM app — prompt topics, retrieved documents, output tone — tracked reference-window against current-window. Next up: when the model itself starts making things up.
